title: Gate in a circuit layer
statement: Let $C$ be a directed acyclic Boolean circuit with $n$ input nodes, an ordered list of $m$ gates, and an output node. Assume each gate has distinct input arguments and every NOT gate has exactly one argument. For an integer $d$ with $0 \le d \le m$ and a node $u$ in layer $d+1$, define a gate whose input wires come from layer $d$ as follows: if $d<m$ and the circuit node represented by $u$ has index less than $n+d$, the gate copies that node's value; otherwise, it is the gate at position $d$, with its arguments wired to their corresponding nodes in layer $d$. When $d=m$, the gate copies the circuit's output node.
hypotheses_covered: C is a DAG circuit with n input nodes

each NOT gate has exactly one argument
d is an integer with 0 ≤ d ≤ the number of gates
u is a node in layer d+1
